 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the appellant/3rd respondent in O.P (MV) No.875 of 2009 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pathanamthitta.
The respondents herein are the appellants before the tribunal.

2. According to the respondents/claimants, on 16.03.2009 at about 09.00 pm, the deceased, a pedestrian was hit down by a motorcycle bearing reg. no KL-33-9545 ridden by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of the accident, he sustained serious injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The claimants who are the widow, son and the mother of the deceased,
approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 9,76,000/-, limited to 8,00,000/-.
3. Respondents 1 to 3 are the driver, owner and the insurer of the offending motorcycle respectively.
The respondent insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy, but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed.
Before the tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced on either side.
Exts. A1
to A9 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 5,80,000/- as compensation under different MACA NO. 549 OF 2015 2025:KER:40664 heads with interest @9% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from the 3rd respondent- insurer.
Challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the insurance company has come up in appeal.

4. Heard the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant insurer and the learned counsel for the claimants/respondents.
5.

The learned standing counsel for the appellant challenged the compensation awarded mainly under the following heads:
Notional income :-

The learned counsel for the respondents/claimants submitted that though the claimants have not filed any cross objection to this appeal, this court has ample powers to fix a just and reasonable income if it is found that the income fixed by the tribunal is on the lower side.
The tribunal has taken only an amount of 4,500/- though an amount of 9,000/- was claimed.

The learned counsel further submitted that as per the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the income ought to have been taken as 7,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that the claimants did not file any cross-objection challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal.
However on a perusal of MACA NO. 549 OF 2015 2025:KER:40664 the award it is seen that the income fixed by the tribunal is on the lower side.

Considering the fact that the motor vehicles act is a welfare legislation, and since there are deductions to be done under the other heads, I find it appropriate to refix the monthly income as 7,000/-.
Since the notional income fixed is 7,000/-, the compensation payable under the said head is recalculated thus: 3,92,000/- (7,000x12x7x2/3).

The tribunal National Insurance Company Limited vs Hamza Beevi on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183932439/
2 has already awarded an amount of 3,24,000/- towards the said head.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs Hamza Beevi on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, there will be an additional amount of 68,000/- under the head loss of dependency.

Compensation for loss of consortium/ loss of love and affection :- The learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium.
Considering the fact that there are three legal heirs.

Going by the judgment in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi &
Ors [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)], I find that the claimants are entitled for a total amount of 1,20,000/- (40,000x3).

entities.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi &
Ors [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Towards loss of consortium, the tribunal has already awarded an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Hence, there will be an additional amount of 20,000/- under the head loss of consortium.

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance MACA NO. 549 OF 2015 2025:KER:40664 company submitted that the tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.1,10,000/- towards loss of love and affection, which is against the principle laid down in the judgment in New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 (5) KLT OnLine 1198 (SC)], wherein it has been held that once compensation is awarded under the head loss of consortium, no amount shall be awarded under the head loss of love and affection, as it would be duplication of compensation.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 (5) KLT OnLine 1198 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence I am inclined to delete Rs.1,10,000/- awarded under the said loss of love and affection.
Compensation for funeral expenses :- The learned standing counsel for the insurance company submitted that, going by the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants are entitled only for a total compensation of 15,000/- under the afore head.
The tribunal has awarded an amount of 25,000/-.
Therefore, there will be a deduction of 10,000/- under the afore head.
Compensation for loss of estate :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that going by the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants are entitled for a total compensation 15,000/- under the afore head.
The tribunal has awarded only an amount of 5,000/-.
Therefore, there will be an additional amount of 10,000/- under the afore head.

Though the appellants claimed enhancement of compensation under other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.

7. Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:

The appellant insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimants shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the appellant insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the claimants at the earliest in accordance with law.
